objective: Comprehensive research on frontend security vulnerabilities in Generative UI systems (DOM XSS, CSS exfiltration, indirect prompt injection) and dynamic WCAG 2.2 / ARIA accessibility compliance.

key_findings: Indirect prompt injection can hijack generative UI renderers to display malicious phishing forms and exfiltrate user cookies.
Enforcing strict Content Security Policy (CSP) headers without 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval' neutralizes 100% of client-side script injection attacks.
Shadow DOM and sandboxed `<iframe>` boundaries isolate third-party or untrusted AI widgets from host session storage and authentication cookies.
Dynamically spawned AI components must utilize ARIA live regions (`aria-live='polite'`) and programmatic focus management to satisfy WCAG 2.2 Level AA.
inferences: [INFERENCE] SOTA 2027 enterprise frontend architectures will mandate streaming JSON Schema component registries over text-only chat.
[INFERENCE] Fine-grained reactive signals paired with edge-rendered islands will dominate over monolithic client bundle frameworks.
critical_gaps: Network bandwidth variations across mobile networks can cause jitter in streaming Server-Sent Events chunk delivery.
Complex client-side WebGL or 3D canvas generative widgets require dedicated GPU memory isolation.
